I do not start from zero. I look at what worked last year, then I adjust a little. My land is only 7.5 mu, so every bag of fertilizer and every spray costs real money, but I still would rather spend a bit more on fertilizer than let the crop go hungry. With well irrigation, I have some control, so I will keep the wheat-maize rotation as the backbone and leave some land for cash vegetables. For wheat and maize, I will stay close to the rates people around me use, but I will split nitrogen so the crop does not run short in the middle stage. For cabbage, chili, and eggplant, I will use improved or hybrid seed if I saw good results in nearby fields, because vegetables bring cash and cannot be handled too stingily. Cabbage needs heavier fertilizer and more water; chili and eggplant need steady topdressing and more sprays because insects and disease come easily. I will plough before the main crops, use rotary tillage for vegetables for convenience, and I will keep yields realistic rather than talking too big.
